outcome.answer: To measure whether a model can learn new rules or knowledge from provided text, you can evaluate how well it aligns to the preferences or criteria implied by the text and whether its outputs remain stable when the evaluation target changes. For example, one approach is to model and test evaluators’ preferences: learn a preference function under assumptions about monotonicity and use a robust algorithm to reduce model mismatch when assumptions are violated [3]. Another approach is to use text- or LLM-generated preference signals to compare slate candidates, then validate that the synthetic preferences align with standard recommendation metrics and preference axioms [4].
